claim: Trypanosoma brucei has a rudimentary actomyosin system consisting of one actin gene and two myosin genes.
source: In the parasitic protist Trypanosoma brucei, a rudimentary actomyosin system consisting of one actin gene and two myosin genes has been retained despite significant investment in the microtubule cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: TbMyo1 can translocate actin filaments in vitro at a velocity of 130 nm/s.
source: The actin filaments were found to move smoothly with a mean gliding velocity of 130 nm/s (Figure 2—video 1, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is directly measured in the in vitro actin filament gliding assay and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: TbMyo1 has a large cytosolic pool, with approximately 40% of TbMyo1 found in the cytosolic fraction.
source: Interestingly, around half of the TbMyo1 (~130 kDa) partitioned into the SN1 fraction, indicating that there is a substantial cytosolic pool.
evidence: This is demonstrated by biochemical fractionation experiments shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: TbMyo1 colocalises with markers for early and late endosomes (TbRab5A and TbRab7, respectively).
source: At the endosomal membranes, TbMyo1 colocalised with markers for early and late endosomes (TbRab5A and TbRab7, respectively), but not with the marker associated with recycling endosomes (TbRab11).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TbMyo1 does not colocalise with the marker associated with recycling endosomes (TbRab11).
source: At the endosomal membranes, TbMyo1 colocalised with markers for early and late endosomes (TbRab5A and TbRab7, respectively), but not with the marker associated with recycling endosomes (TbRab11).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Disruption of the actomyosin system using latrunculin A resulted in a delocalisation of both the actin chromobody signal and an endosomal marker.
source: Disruption of the actomyosin system using the actin-depolymerising drug latrunculin A resulted in a delocalisation of both the actin chromobody signal and an endosomal marker, and was accompanied by a specific loss of endosomal structure.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: Disruption of the actomyosin system using latrunculin A was accompanied by a specific loss of endosomal structure.
source: Disruption of the actomyosin system using the actin-depolymerising drug latrunculin A resulted in a delocalisation of both the actin chromobody signal and an endosomal marker, and was accompanied by a specific loss of endosomal structure.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7C.

claim: The actomyosin system is required for maintaining endosomal integrity in T. brucei.
source: This suggests that the actomyosin system is required for maintaining endosomal integrity in T. brucei.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the latrunculin A experiments.

claim: TbMyo1 is localised to glycosomes.
source: Interestingly, glycosomes (readily identifiable because of their electron-dense lumen) were also regularly labelled with the anti-TbMyo1 antibodies (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is observed in immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4E and confirmed by CLEM in Figure 5C and D.

claim: TbMyo1 is predicted to consist of a large motor domain, a single calmodulin-binding IQ motif, and a membrane-binding FYVE-domain.
source: Based on sequence analysis, TbMyo1 is predicted to consist of a large motor domain (cyan), a single calmodulin-binding IQ motif (yellow) and a membrane-binding FYVE-domain (magenta) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and structural prediction shown in Figure 2A.

claim: TbMyo1 eluted together with human calmodulin during size-exclusion chromatography.
source: TbMyo1 (130 kDa) eluted together with human calmodulin in the 11.5–12.5 ml elution fractions.
evidence: This is shown in the SDS-PAGE analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: TbMyo1 is mainly detected in the posterior region of the cell between the nucleus and the kinetoplast.
source: After expansion of wild-type T. brucei cells, endogenous TbMyo1 was mainly detected in the posterior region of the cell between the nucleus (N) and the mitochondrial genome (kinetoplast, K) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is observed in expansion microscopy experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: TbMyo1 does not substantially overlap with the ER chaperone BiP.
source: No substantial overlap was seen between TbMyo1 and BiP (Figure 3BI,II). Accordingly, the correlation between the two proteins in the population was weak (ρ = 0.35) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalisation experiments and correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: TbMyo1 and the Golgi marker GRASP displayed no overlap.
source: Similarly, TbMyo1 and the Golgi marker GRASP displayed no overlap (Figure 3BIII,IV) and weak correlation (ρ = 0.30) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalisation experiments and correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: TbMyo1 and the lysosome marker p67 were frequently observed in close proximity but did not overlap.
source: TbMyo1 and the lysosome marker p67 were frequently observed in close proximity in the posterior region of the cell but did not overlap despite the TbMyo1 signal being close to and sometimes surrounding the p67 signal (Figure 3BV,VI).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: TbMyo1 partially overlaps with the endocytic cargo BSA.
source: The BSA signal was mainly found in a single globular cluster in the posterior region of the cell, which seemed to partially overlap with TbMyo1 (Figure 3DI).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cargo uptake experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: TbMyo1 has a more substantial overlap with transferrin compared to BSA.
source: The transferrin signal was more widely distributed and seemed to have a more substantial overlap with TbMyo1 (Figure 3DII).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cargo uptake experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The majority of TbMyo1 gold signals (57%) were found in the cytoplasm in immuno-electron microscopy experiments.
source: While the majority of TbMyo1 gold signals were found in the cytoplasm (57%), equal proportions (15%) were found at glycosomes and endosomes, with smaller amounts at the flagellar pocket (8%) and on vesicles (5%) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is quantified from immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 15% of TbMyo1 gold signals were found at glycosomes in immuno-electron microscopy experiments.
source: While the majority of TbMyo1 gold signals were found in the cytoplasm (57%), equal proportions (15%) were found at glycosomes and endosomes, with smaller amounts at the flagellar pocket (8%) and on vesicles (5%) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is quantified from immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 15% of TbMyo1 gold signals were found at endosomes in immuno-electron microscopy experiments.
source: While the majority of TbMyo1 gold signals were found in the cytoplasm (57%), equal proportions (15%) were found at glycosomes and endosomes, with smaller amounts at the flagellar pocket (8%) and on vesicles (5%) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is quantified from immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: TbMyo1 is clustered adjacent to the lysosome.
source: The TbMyo1 signal (magenta) was frequently clustered on one side of the lysosomal signal but did not overlap with it.
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLEM experiments shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: An anti-actin chromobody can be used to visualise actin in T. brucei.
source: The anti-actin chromobody was first subcloned into a trypanosome tetracycline-inducible expression vector and a stable cell line was generated.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful expression and localisation of the chromobody shown in Figure 6.

claim: The anti-actin chromobody signal is restricted to the posterior region of cells between the nucleus and kinetoplast.
source: At the single-cell level, a fluorescent chromobody signal was only detectable in the presence of tetracycline and was restricted to the posterior region of cells between the nucleus and kinetoplast (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by widefield microscopy shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Treatment with latrunculin A disrupts the chromobody signal.
source: While low concentrations (0.2 μM) of LatA showed a slight delocalisation of the chromobody signal, high concentrations (2 μM) resulted in a strong delocalisation or even loss of the chromobody signal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by latrunculin A treatment experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: TbMyo1 and actin strongly overlap in the posterior part of the cell.
source: Next, the extent of overlap between TbMyo1 and actin was assessed. The signals strongly overlapped in the posterior part of the cell (Figure 6D). This was reflected in strong correlation between the signals in the population (ρ = 0.63) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 6D and correlation analysis in Figure 6E.

claim: Latrunculin A treatment results in aberrant cell morphologies.
source: Longer incubation with LatA resulted in aberrant cell morphologies and an increasingly diffuse EP1-GFP signal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by latrunculin A treatment experiments shown in Figure 7A.

claim: After 1 hr of LatA incubation, 50% of the cells displayed morphological changes.
source: After 1 hr of LatA incubation, 50% of the cells displayed morphological changes, including swelling of the cell body in the posterior part and even complete rounding of the cell (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is quantified from latrunculin A treatment experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Latrunculin A treatment results in a complete loss of endosomal integrity.
source: Examination of the ultrastructure of the endosomal system at early timepoints (≤60 min LatA incubation) revealed a complete loss of endosomal integrity, resulting in large membrane vesicles filling the space between the flagellar pocket and the lysosome (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electron microscopy of latrunculin A-treated cells shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The Golgi complex structure is preserved after latrunculin A treatment.
source: The preservation of the Golgi complex structure in its entirety, as well as the continuing invagination of clathrin-coated pits and presence of clathrin-coated vesicles at the flagellar pocket, underscored the specificity of this phenotype (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is observed in electron microscopy of latrunculin A-treated cells shown in Figure 7C.

claim: TbMyo21 exhibited minimal expression in both BSF and procyclic form cells.
source: TbMyo21 was found to have extremely low expression levels in both BSF and procyclic life cycle stages, however.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblotting shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and 2D.

claim: TbMyo21 appeared to be non-essential for BSF cell growth.
source: In addition, the protein could not be confidently localised using widefield microscopy and RNAi experiments showed that it appeared to be non-essential for BSF cell growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNAi growth curve experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F.

claim: TbMyo1 expression is downregulated in the procyclic life cycle stage.
source: Of note, preliminary data indicate downregulation of TbMyo1 expression in the procyclic life cycle stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E), consistent with earlier proteomic experiments (Tinti and Ferguson, 2022).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblotting shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E and supported by a citation.

claim: The velocity of TbMyo1 (130 nm/s) is significantly faster than the approximately 10–50 nm/s measured for some mammalian class I myosins.
source: The in vitro motility assays indicated that TbMyo1 can translocate filamentous actin with a mean translocation velocity of 130 nm/s, which is significantly faster than the approximately 10–50 nm/s measured for some mammalian class I myosins (Giese et al., 2021; Pyrpassopoulos et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to comparative studies.

claim: Trypanosomatids are the most divergent eukaryotes that still retain an actomyosin system with associated regulatory proteins.
source: Recently, it was shown that trypanosomatids – a family of unicellular parasites – are the most divergent eukaryotes that still retain an actomyosin system with associated regulatory proteins (Kotila et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: T. brucei bloodstream forms express a surface coat of 5 × 10^6 VSG dimers.
source: To evade the mammalian host's immune system, T. brucei bloodstream forms (BSFs) express a surface coat of variable surface glycoproteins (VSGs) consisting of 5 × 106 VSG dimers (Bartossek et al., 2017; Cross, 1975; Jackson et al., 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The VSG cell surface pool is turned over within 12 min.
source: Measurements of the kinetics of VSG endocytosis and recycling revealed that the VSG cell surface pool is turned over within 12 min (Engstler et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Surface-bound antibodies are internalised and colocalise with lysosome markers within 2 min.
source: Surface-bound antibodies are internalised and colocalise with lysosome markers within 2 min (Engstler et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The endosomal system of T. brucei forms an interconnected membrane network rather than separate compartments.
source: It was recently shown that the endosomal system of T. brucei has a remarkably complex architecture (Link et al., 2023). Rather than being divided into separate compartments, the system forms an interconnected membrane network.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion of actin in BSF T. brucei resulted in a rapid cell division arrest, loss of endocytic activity, and ultimately cell death.
source: Previous work on T. brucei actin showed that its depletion in BSFs resulted in a rapid cell division arrest, loss of endocytic activity, and ultimately cell death (García-Salcedo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: T. brucei filamentous actin has not been visualised by phalloidin binding.
source: Interestingly, T. brucei filamentous actin has not been visualised by phalloidin binding.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Filamentous actin in trypanosomes may be short and dynamic.
source: This suggests that filamentous actin in trypanosomes may be short and dynamic, as is the case in Plasmodium (Schmitz et al., 2005; Schüler et al., 2005), and was recently shown in the related trypanosomatid parasite Leishmania (Kotila et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: TbMyo1 partially colocalised with endocytic cargo, late endosomes, and the lysosome in BSF T. brucei cells.
source: In BSF T. brucei cells, TbMyo1 partially colocalised with endocytic cargo, late endosomes, and the lysosome (Spitznagel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion of TbMyo1 resulted in the inhibition of cargo uptake and an enlargement of the flagellar pocket.
source: In addition, the depletion of TbMyo1 resulted in the inhibition of cargo uptake and an enlargement of the flagellar pocket (Spitznagel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion or drug-induced disruption of actin resulted in a decreased and more diffuse TbMyo1 signal.
source: Although a direct colocalisation of actin and TbMyo1 was not demonstrated, the depletion or drug-induced disruption of actin resulted in a decreased and more diffuse TbMyo1 signal.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to Spitznagel et al., 2010.

claim: Knockdown of the class XXI myosin in Leishmania was reported to be lethal, with defects in flagellar assembly and a loss of intracellular trafficking.
source: In Leishmania, knockdown of the class XXI myosin was reported to be lethal, with defects in flagellar assembly and a loss of intracellular trafficking (Katta et al., 2009; Katta et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The predicted FYVE domain in the TbMyo1 tail domain is predicted to mediate binding to PI(3)P lipids.
source: Furthermore, the predicted FYVE domain in the TbMyo1 tail domain is predicted to mediate binding to PI(3)P lipids, which are enriched in endosomal membranes in other organisms (Marat and Haucke, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Preliminary data indicate that the FYVE domain of TbMyo1 can specifically bind to PI(3)P.
source: Preliminary data indicate that this FYVE domain can indeed specifically bind to PI(3)P (C. Veigel and F. Zierhut, unpublished observations).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and attributed to unpublished observations.

claim: The actomyosin system has often been associated with membrane manipulation in different organisms.
source: The actomyosin system has often been associated with membrane manipulation in different organisms (Costa et al., 2020; Eitzen, 2003; Khatibzadeh et al., 2013; Khanal Lamichhane et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: In Drosophila, endosomes can organise F-actin and endosomal actin can affect subcellular tube growth and integrity.
source: Interestingly, it has recently been shown that in Drosophila endosomes can organise F-actin and that endosomal actin can affect subcellular tube growth and integrity (Ríos-Barrera and Leptin, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: TbMyo1 was previously found in a glycosomal proteome obtained by mass spectrometry.
source: TbMyo1 was previously found in a glycosomal proteome obtained by mass spectrometry (see Supplementary Material, Table S2, proteins only detected in BSFs in Vertommen et al., 2008), providing independent validation of the ultrastructural localisation observed here.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: A connection to the cytoskeleton has been described as a requirement for peroxisome function, inheritance, and maintenance in plants, yeast, and mammalian cells.
source: While a connection to the cytoskeleton has been described as a requirement for peroxisome function, inheritance, and maintenance in plants, yeast, and mammalian cells (Neuhaus et al., 2016), nothing has been reported regarding a connection to the cytoskeleton for glycosomes in trypanosomatids.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Recent work in mammalian cells has suggested that actin is recruited to endocytic sites primarily when endocytosis stalls.
source: Recent work in mammalian cells has suggested that actin is recruited to endocytic sites primarily when endocytosis stalls, and a similar mechanism could conceivably be at work here (Jin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The remaining portion of TbMyo1 (after cytosolic extraction) predominantly partitioned into the cytoskeleton-associated P2 fraction.
source: The remaining material (P1) predominantly partitioned into the cytoskeleton-associated P2 fraction (Figure 1B, bottom panel, green).
evidence: This is demonstrated by biochemical fractionation experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and BiP was weak (ρ = 0.35).
source: No substantial overlap was seen between TbMyo1 and BiP (Figure 3BI,II). Accordingly, the correlation between the two proteins in the population was weak (ρ = 0.35) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and GRASP was weak (ρ = 0.30).
source: Similarly, TbMyo1 and the Golgi marker GRASP displayed no overlap (Figure 3BIII,IV) and weak correlation (ρ = 0.30) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and p67 was moderate (ρ = 0.43).
source: The correlation between the two proteins was moderate (ρ=0.43) compared to the ER and Golgi markers and showed a much larger spread of values (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and BSA was very weak (ρ = 0.17).
source: Surprisingly, despite the clear visual overlap of cargo marker and TbMyo1 signals, the correlations were very weak (ρ = 0.17 and 0.20, respectively) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and transferrin was very weak (ρ = 0.20).
source: Surprisingly, despite the clear visual overlap of cargo marker and TbMyo1 signals, the correlations were very weak (ρ = 0.17 and 0.20, respectively) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The correlation between TbMyo1 and actin was strong (ρ = 0.63).
source: This was reflected in strong correlation between the signals in the population (ρ = 0.63) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is quantified from colocalisation experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: At longer incubation times with LatA, no cells displaying a normal morphology were observed.
source: At longer incubation times, no cells displaying a normal morphology were observed.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: Even after 30–60 min of LatA incubation, which led to the complete disruption of the endosomal system, the parasites remained motile.
source: It is noteworthy that even after 30–60 min of LatA incubation, which led to the complete disruption of the endosomal system, the parasites remained motile.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: An enlargement of the flagellar pocket was not observed in most cells during 30-60 min of LatA incubation.
source: Moreover, an enlargement of the flagellar pocket was not observed in most cells during this period.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: Depletion of TbMyo1 caused a very penetrant phenotype, with most of the cells already rounded-up after 24 hr of induction.
source: Depletion of TbMyo1 caused a very penetrant phenotype, with most of the cells already rounded-up after 24 hr of induction (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNAi experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cells with less deranged morphology after TbMyo1 depletion were still capable of internalising BSA and trafficking it to a lysosome-adjacent compartment.
source: These rounded-up cells are not phenotypically informative, but the cells with a less deranged morphology were still capable of internalising BSA and trafficking it to a lysosome-adjacent compartment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by BSA uptake experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In TbMyo1-depleted cells, clathrin-coated vesicles in the cytoplasm and clathrin patches on the flagellar pocket membrane were frequently observed.
source: As in the LatA experiments and consistent with the BSA uptake experiments, clathrin-coated vesicles in the cytoplasm and clathrin patches on the flagellar pocket membrane were frequently observed, suggesting that endocytosis was not strongly affected (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is observed in electron microscopy of TbMyo1-depleted cells shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The large cytosolic fraction of TbMyo1 could potentially indicate the molecules adopting an auto-inhibited 'foldback' configuration.
source: The substantial cytosolic fraction of TbMyo1 could potentially indicate the molecules adopting an auto-inhibited 'foldback' configuration (Yang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation and supported by a citation.

claim: The relatively high velocity of TbMyo1 might indicate that it is participating in intracellular trafficking of BSF T. brucei and functioning as an active motor rather than a static tether.
source: This relatively high velocity might indicate that TbMyo1 is participating in intracellular trafficking of BSF T. brucei and functioning as an active motor rather than a static tether.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the in vitro motility data.

claim: The actomyosin system in trypanosomes primarily functions in post-endocytic trafficking events.
source: The consistent localisation of TbMyo1 at or close to the endosomal network and lysosomes, coupled with the fact that neither TbMyo1 nor actin accumulated near the flagellar pocket, suggests that the actomyosin system in trypanosomes primarily functions in post-endocytic trafficking events.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the localisation data.

claim: The actomyosin system either generates or helps maintain the architecture of the trypanosome endosomal system.
source: Thus, it could be that the actomyosin system either generates or helps maintain the architecture of the trypanosome endosomal system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: TbMyo1 is unlikely to be essential for endocytosis to occur.
source: It was surprising that no strong or consistent signal was seen for either TbMyo1 or actin at the flagellar pocket, and it might be possible that neither are essential for endocytosis to occur.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on the localisation data.

claim: The primary focus and function of trypanosome actin and TbMyo1 is centred on the endosomal system.
source: Regardless, it seems clear that the primary focus and function of trypanosome actin and TbMyo1 is centred on the endosomal system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Control cells (0 hr LatA incubation) mostly (~85%) exhibited normal morphology.
source: Control cells, harvested and fixed after 0 hr of LatA incubation, mostly (~85%) exhibited normal morphology.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: The EP1-GFP fluorescence in control cells was concentrated in the posterior region of the cell and revealed a variable number of high-intensity signals.
source: The EP1-GFP fluorescence in the controls was concentrated in the posterior region of the cell and revealed a variable number of high-intensity signals, surrounded and connected by weaker signals.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: The morphological changes caused by LatA were accompanied by a redistribution of the EP1-GFP fluorescence signals.
source: These morphological changes were accompanied by a redistribution of the EP1-GFP fluorescence signals. Instead of being confined to the posterior region, the EP1-GFP signals increasingly spread throughout the entire cytoplasm.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing latrunculin A treatment experiments.

claim: The immuno-labelled structures observed in electron microscopy were variable and included both vesicles and cisternae with circular or elongated shapes.
source: The morphology of the immuno-labelled structures was variable and included both vesicles and cisternae with circular or elongated shapes (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is observed in immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4A-D.

claim: The vesicles observed in electron microscopy were found in different sizes ranging from 30 to 100 nm.
source: The vesicles were found in different sizes ranging from 30 to 100 nm, while the elongated membrane structures were between 20 and 30 nm thick and up to 1 μm long.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing immuno-electron microscopy observations.

claim: The elongated membrane structures observed in electron microscopy were between 20 and 30 nm thick and up to 1 μm long.
source: The vesicles were found in different sizes ranging from 30 to 100 nm, while the elongated membrane structures were between 20 and 30 nm thick and up to 1 μm long.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing immuno-electron microscopy observations.

claim: The 5 nm gold particles (BSA) were observed inside the membrane structures, confirming their endosomal identity.
source: The 5 nm gold particles were observed inside the membrane structures, confirming their endosomal identity (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This is observed in immuno-electron microscopy experiments with BSA-gold shown in Figure 4F-H.

claim: Gold particles (BSA) were found inside coated vesicles and abundantly in the lysosome.
source: In addition, gold particles were found inside coated vesicles and abundantly in the lysosome (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is observed in immuno-electron microscopy experiments with BSA-gold shown in Figure 4H.

claim: 8% of TbMyo1 gold signals were found at the flagellar pocket in immuno-electron microscopy experiments.
source: While the majority of TbMyo1 gold signals were found in the cytoplasm (57%), equal proportions (15%) were found at glycosomes and endosomes, with smaller amounts at the flagellar pocket (8%) and on vesicles (5%) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is quantified from immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 5% of TbMyo1 gold signals were found on vesicles in immuno-electron microscopy experiments.
source: While the majority of TbMyo1 gold signals were found in the cytoplasm (57%), equal proportions (15%) were found at glycosomes and endosomes, with smaller amounts at the flagellar pocket (8%) and on vesicles (5%) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is quantified from immuno-electron microscopy experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: The TbMyo1 localisation matched the previously reported localisation of actin in trypanosomes.
source: This matched the previously reported localisation of actin in trypanosomes (García-Salcedo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The distribution pattern of the chromobody signal was consistent across cells despite cell-to-cell variation in expression level.
source: Although there was cell-to-cell variation in the expression level of the chromobody, the distribution pattern was consistent (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The TbMyo1 distribution was the same in uninduced and induced chromobody cells.
source: Importantly, the TbMyo1 distribution was the same in uninduced and induced cells, indicating that its localisation was not affected by the expression of the chromobody.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The colocalising area of TbMyo1 and actin was often up to 1 μm away from the kinetoplast/flagellar pocket region.
source: Of note, the colocalising area was often up to 1 μm away from the kinetoplast/flagellar pocket region (Figure 6F) and only a minority of cells showed a signal for either TbMyo1, actin, or both adjacent to the kinetoplast (Figure 6FI,II).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Only a minority of cells showed a signal for either TbMyo1, actin, or both adjacent to the kinetoplast.
source: Of note, the colocalising area was often up to 1 μm away from the kinetoplast/flagellar pocket region (Figure 6F) and only a minority of cells showed a signal for either TbMyo1, actin, or both adjacent to the kinetoplast (Figure 6FI,II).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The actomyosin system is not constitutively present at the flagellar pocket.
source: These observations suggested that the actomyosin system is not constitutively present at the flagellar pocket.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the localisation data.

claim: TbMyo1 was previously found to be associated with the endosomal system using non-physiological cargoes (lectins) as markers.
source: TbMyo1 had previously been suggested to overlap with the endosomal system, but this work was conducted using non-physiological cargoes (lectins) as markers (Spitznagel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The close juxtaposition of ERES and the Golgi apparatus in T. brucei could provide a rationale for why a motor protein like TbMyo1 might be dispensable for mediating transport between these organelles.
source: The close juxtaposition of endoplasmic reticulum exit sites (ERES) and the Golgi apparatus in T. brucei could provide a rationale for why a motor protein like TbMyo1 might be dispensable for mediating transport between these organelles (Sealey-Cardona et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation and supported by a citation.

claim: Secretory material in T. brucei might move in bulk from the Golgi to the endosomal system.
source: Recently, a potential mechanism was discussed in which secretory material in T. brucei might move in bulk from the Golgi to the endosomal system (Link et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The endosomal network serves as a central sorting hub for both secretory and endocytic cargo in T. brucei.
source: In this model, it is the endosomal network that serves as a central sorting hub for both secretory and endocytic cargo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as part of a proposed model.

claim: Correlation and co-occurrence are different concepts in colocalisation analysis.
source: This highlights a potentially important point which is often glossed over in colocalisation analyses – correlation and co-occurrence are different concepts, although both are measures of colocalisation (Aaron et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Two signals can be strongly correlated even if they do not exhibit much spatial overlap/co-occurrence.
source: Thus, it is possible for two signals to be strongly correlated even if they do not exhibit much spatial overlap/co-occurrence.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation of colocalisation concepts.

claim: Two signals can exhibit strong overlap/co-occurrence but low correlation.
source: Conversely, and as here, two signals can exhibit strong overlap/co-occurrence but low correlation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation of colocalisation concepts.

claim: TbMyo1 and cargo are present in the same locations (cargo-containing endosomes), but in different proportions.
source: The incidence of zero-versus-nonzero values in the two channels will have lowered the correlation coefficient, and in this sense, the correlation coefficients are giving a hint of what the immuno-electron microscopy later confirmed: that the TbMyo1 and cargo are present in the same locations (i.e. cargo-containing endosomes), but in different proportions (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the correlation data.

claim: The existence of a large cytosolic fraction at steady state might suggest that TbMyo1 is very dynamic, with a high turnover on the organelles it is associated with.
source: The existence of a large cytosolic fraction at steady state might also suggest that TbMyo1 is very dynamic, with a high turnover on the organelles it is associated with.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: The in vitro motility assay conditions do not replicate the highly complex and dynamic cytoplasmic environment within a trypanosome cell.
source: It should be stressed, however, that this study has not investigated any of TbMyo1's biochemical or mechanical activities in vivo, so this remains a hypothesis for now. The in vitro motility assay conditions obviously do not replicate the highly complex and dynamic cytoplasmic environment within a trypanosome cell, and multiple regulatory mechanisms, binding partners, and maybe even membrane interactions (see below) will all come into play.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a caveat to the in vitro data.

claim: This study has not investigated any of TbMyo1's biochemical or mechanical activities in vivo.
source: It should be stressed, however, that this study has not investigated any of TbMyo1's biochemical or mechanical activities in vivo, so this remains a hypothesis for now.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the study.

claim: This study has not rigorously investigated a direct functional role for TbMyo1 in endomembrane function.
source: It should be stressed that the present study has not rigorously investigated a direct functional role for TbMyo1 in endomembrane function, and any associations that are drawn based on the data here are necessarily speculative.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the study.

claim: Further experiments using the TbMyo1 RNAi cell line will be needed to explore the functional role of TbMyo1 in more detail.
source: Further experiments using the TbMyo1 RNAi cell line will be needed to explore this point in more detail.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a future direction.

claim: Nothing is known about the lipid composition of endosomal membranes in trypanosomes.
source: So far, nothing is known about the lipid composition of endosomal membranes in trypanosomes, but the presence of a FYVE domain and the enrichment of TbMyo1 at endosomal membranes suggests PI(3)P lipids in the endosomes of trypanosomes too.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The expression of the FYVE domain conjugated to GFP might be a useful tool to visualise PI(3)P-enriched membranes in T. brucei.
source: If so, the expression of the FYVE domain conjugated to GFP might be a useful tool to visualise PI(3)P-enriched membranes in T. brucei.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: The link between glycosomes and TbMyo1 was unexpected and merits further investigation.
source: This link between glycosomes and TbMyo1 was unexpected and merits further investigation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Nothing has been reported regarding a connection to the cytoskeleton for glycosomes in trypanosomatids.
source: While a connection to the cytoskeleton has been described as a requirement for peroxisome function, inheritance, and maintenance in plants, yeast, and mammalian cells (Neuhaus et al., 2016), nothing has been reported regarding a connection to the cytoskeleton for glycosomes in trypanosomatids.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Actin and TbMyo1 had not been imaged simultaneously in T. brucei until this study.
source: Until now, however, TbMyo1 and actin had not been imaged simultaneously in T. brucei.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The ability to observe actin distributions in living trypanosome cells will be invaluable for future studies of its intracellular dynamics.
source: The ability to observe actin distributions in living trypanosome cells will undoubtedly be invaluable for future studies of its intracellular dynamics, although further optimisation is still required.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a future direction.

claim: Further optimisation of the chromobody system is still required.
source: The ability to observe actin distributions in living trypanosome cells will undoubtedly be invaluable for future studies of its intracellular dynamics, although further optimisation is still required.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: It will be important to do a time-course experiment to determine the shortest incubation time required for maximal expression of the chromobody.
source: It will be important in the future to do a time-course experiment to determine the shortest incubation time required for maximal expression of the chromobody.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a future direction.

claim: The overnight inductions used for the chromobody are undoubtedly excessive.
source: The overnight inductions used here are undoubtedly excessive, and some cells with abnormal morphology could be observed at low frequency.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation.

claim: Some cells with abnormal morphology could be observed at low frequency after overnight chromobody induction.
source: The overnight inductions used here are undoubtedly excessive, and some cells with abnormal morphology could be observed at low frequency.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The strong overlap between TbMyo1 and actin suggests that actin is highly decorated with TbMyo1.
source: As TbMyo1 is a motor protein, the strong overlap with actin was expected and suggests that actin is highly decorated with TbMyo1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the colocalisation data.

claim: The number and intensity of signal spots for TbMyo1 and actin varied from cell to cell.
source: Nevertheless, the number and intensity of signal spots varied from cell to cell.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The actomyosin system in T. brucei is highly dynamic.
source: Coupled with the relatively high velocity measured of TbMyo1 on actin, this suggests that the actomyosin system in T. brucei is highly dynamic.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: The obvious next step would be the acquisition of the dynamics of the different endosomal marker proteins and the cytoskeleton in vivo.
source: The obvious next step would be the acquisition of the dynamics of the different endosomal marker proteins and the cytoskeleton in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a future direction.

claim: It might be possible that neither actin nor TbMyo1 are essential for endocytosis to occur.
source: It was surprising that no strong or consistent signal was seen for either TbMyo1 or actin at the flagellar pocket, and it might be possible that neither are essential for endocytosis to occur.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: A similar mechanism to mammalian cells (where actin is recruited to endocytic sites primarily when endocytosis stalls) could conceivably be at work in trypanosomes.
source: Recent work in mammalian cells has suggested that actin is recruited to endocytic sites primarily when endocytosis stalls, and a similar mechanism could conceivably be at work here (Jin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation and supported by a citation.

claim: TbMyo21 is unlikely to be a viable drug target in T. brucei.
source: Due to its exceedingly low expression levels and non-essential role in BSF T. brucei, TbMyo21 is unlikely to be a viable drug target, in contrast to its homologue in Leishmania (Trivedi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the expression and RNAi data.

claim: The discrepancy in TbMyo1 expression levels between BSF and PCF cells compared to the previous study is most likely due to the stronger signal obtained with the new anti-TbMyo1 antibodies.
source: This finding differs with the previous study, where no change in TbMyo1 expression levels was observed after differentiation (Spitznagel et al., 2010). The discrepancy is most likely due to the stronger signal obtained in the present study with the new anti-TbMyo1 antibodies, although a more rigorous experiment using a loading control with identical expression levels in the two life cycle stages is still needed.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: A more rigorous experiment using a loading control with identical expression levels in the two life cycle stages is still needed to confirm TbMyo1 downregulation in PCF cells.
source: The discrepancy is most likely due to the stronger signal obtained in the present study with the new anti-TbMyo1 antibodies, although a more rigorous experiment using a loading control with identical expression levels in the two life cycle stages is still needed.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation.

claim: The actomyosin system is not as critical for the viability of procyclic cells, which have a much lower rate of membrane trafficking than the BSF life cycle stage.
source: This nonetheless suggests that the actomyosin system is not as critical for the viability of procyclic cells, which have a much lower rate of membrane trafficking than the BSF life cycle stage.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the expression data.

claim: TbMyo1 might be important only in cell cycle stages that cannot be cultivated in vitro, such as epimastigotes.
source: It remains possible that TbMyo21 might be important only in cell cycle stages that cannot be cultivated in vitro, such as epimastigotes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation about TbMyo21.

claim: This represents the first use of CLEM on cryosections in trypanosomes.
source: This represents the first use of CLEM on cryosections in trypanosomes, confirming it as a viable experimental approach for T. brucei.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: CLEM on cryosections is a viable experimental approach for T. brucei.
source: This represents the first use of CLEM on cryosections in trypanosomes, confirming it as a viable experimental approach for T. brucei.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the successful experiments.

claim: Actin was previously visualised in T. brucei using an anti-actin polyclonal antibody.
source: Actin was previously visualised in T. brucei using an anti-actin polyclonal antibody (García-Salcedo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The anti-actin chromobody was previously used to visualise actin in living Toxoplasma cells.
source: The anti-actin chromobody used here was previously used to visualise actin in living Toxoplasma cells (Periz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: It had not been tested whether the anti-actin chromobody could be used in trypanosomatids before this study.
source: It had not been tested whether it could be used in trypanosomatids, however.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The anti-actin chromobody could potentially enable the study of dynamic actin localisations in live cells in the future.
source: If the anti-actin chromobody could be shown to work in trypanosomatids, this would potentially enable the study of dynamic actin localisations in live cells in the future.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as speculation.
